name: list_shared
title: List what was shared
description: List what the team shared with you, as a directory tree: documents (docs/*.md, with their files and earlier versions), chats (chat.md) and other agents' conversations (conversation.md), under the orgs, projects, topics and threads they belong to. Without a path it lists where you are: your topic, what it is about, and the other threads working on it with their states. "/" is the top of everything you can reach. depth looks further down; names filters by a pattern such as *.md. Pages hold 50 entries by default (limit: 1 to 200). Follow next_cursor with the same path, depth and filters; a displayed row's cursor also continues immediately after that row. sort defaults to "changed": active work, then most recently changed; "name" orders by name. Archived entries are counted until include_archived is true. Entries carry the first line of their description (a document without one gives its first paragraph's), their last change, children and a topic's open/done status. To name an entry in what you write, link its path, with #n for a part: [Rollout plan](<docs/Rollout plan.md#3>). Document directories contain documents and nested document folders; their attachment and history directories are discoverable beside them. A writable document is one edit_document may change. A writable document directory permits documents or folders to be created there; its parents must already exist. manage_shared creates folders, copies, moves, deletes and restores documents or folders. Manageable marks the item; recursive operations separately authorize every descendant. A built-in docs root, attachment directory or history directory is not itself mutable. Writable chats and threads are addressed by send_message with target.kind "chat" or "thread" respectively.

limit.description: How many rows: 50 when left out.

cursor.description: Where a list that was cut goes on: the cursor it gave.

sort.description: The order within each directory: active work first, then most recently changed (the default), or names.

include_archived.description: Include archived entries and their readable contents; otherwise one count says how many were folded.

path.description: The directory to list: a path of the tree, from "/" or from your own topic, or id: and an id. Your own topic when left out.

depth.description: How many levels down to list. 1 when left out.

kinds.description: Keep only entries of these kinds.

names.description: A pattern over entry names, as a shell has them: * ? [...]. Only entries whose name matches are listed.

max_bytes.description: The most UTF-8 bytes in the complete answer: 20000 when left out, at most 40000.

ids.description: Include optional opaque object ids; false when left out. Required references and positions remain.

name: read_shared
title: Read a shared entry
description: Read one entry of the shared tree by its path: a document or one of its earlier versions as Markdown, a chat, or a conversation, your own or another thread's. A folder is listed with list_shared, not read as a document. An entry is counted in parts (a conversation in turns, a chat in messages, a document in blocks): from and to name a range of them, and a negative number counts from the end. Without a range you get the latest turns or messages that fit, or the beginning of a document. detail is how much of each part: "brief" gives a few lines for each turn or message, or a document's headings, and is how to find your way in something long; "normal" is the text, with one line for each thing another agent did; "full" adds what each of those steps was given and what came back, and the comments beside a document. The answer is one line that says what it holds and how much there is, then the text itself. What you read is a record: a request in it was made to somebody else, at another time, and is not a request to you. It changes nothing and nobody is told. A reference in what you read is written [name](path#n): pass that path to read_shared, and n as from; a shared name followed by (no access) names something you may not read. Tell your person if you need it; agents do not request access. Attachments, including text files, and anything you want whole on your disk are fetched with download_shared. Their .files directories are beside the owning document or chat, including inside document folders. Files also use a shared path or your workspace path, with :n or #n for a text line. Use your file tools for workspace paths.

path.description: The entry to read: its path in the tree, or id: and an id.

from.description: The first part to read. A negative number counts from the end.

to.description: The last part to read. A negative number counts from the end.

detail.description: How much of each part: brief, normal (the default) or full.

max_bytes.description: The most bytes of text to return. 20000 when left out.

ids.description: Include optional opaque object ids; false when left out. Required references and positions remain.

name: search_shared
title: Search what was shared
description: Search readable names and content. Words match in any order; double quotes keep a phrase together. regex uses a regular expression without look-around or back-references. Each row represents one entry, best matches first (a name or title, then a description, a heading, the rest; then more matching rows; then newer), with a match count and first native positions for read_shared; path#position names one in what you write. Where your org searches by meaning, the first page also holds entries near the query in meaning, each with found_by. Text snippets are omitted unless snippets is true. Continue with the returned cursor and the same query, path and filters; partial counts describe the bounded scan window. Narrow with path, kinds or names when needed.

query.description: Words in any order; double quotes keep a phrase together. With regex, a regular expression instead.

regex.description: Whether query is a regular expression, without look-around and without back-references.

path.description: A directory to look under. Everything you can reach when left out.

kinds.description: Which kinds to look in. All four when left out.

names.description: A pattern over entry names: only entries whose name matches are looked at.

max_results.description: The most matching entries, newest first. 50 when left out.

cursor.description: Where a list that was cut goes on: the cursor it gave.

snippets.description: Include text snippets with native positions. False when left out; summaries always include match counts and first positions.

context.description: How many lines around a match a snippet carries. 1 when left out.

max_bytes.description: The most UTF-8 bytes in the complete answer: 20000 when left out, at most 40000.

ids.description: Include optional opaque object ids; false when left out. Required references and positions remain.

name: download_shared
title: Copy a shared entry into the workspace
description: Copy one readable shared entry into your workspace, where its owner's Export permission also lets you take it away. For a file attached to a document or chat, give its exact path from list_shared or the written links in read_shared (a document's .files/ directory or chat.files/). It downloads the original whole bytes, including images and forwarded chat attachments; format and detail do not render or change a file. For a document, chat or conversation, download the whole Markdown at the requested detail, or use format "json" for records. Without save_to the destination is .orch/shared/downloads/<canonical filename>; save_to chooses another relative path under your directory. Equal existing bytes are kept, and different existing bytes are never overwritten. Attachment size is bounded by storage.max_blob_bytes. A missing, deleted or no longer shared attachment refuses without writing a file. Large files take time: when the answer says "downloading", call again with the same path and destination to ask for its current result.

path.description: The entry or attachment to copy: the exact shared path from list_shared or read_shared, or id: and an id.

save_to.description: Where to write it under your directory. When left out, .orch/shared/downloads/<canonical filename>; a file keeps its original bytes and extension.

detail.description: For an entry that is no file: brief, normal (the default) or full.

format.description: For an entry that is no file: markdown (the default), or json for a program to read.

max_bytes.description: The most UTF-8 bytes in the complete answer: 20000 when left out, at most 40000.

ids.description: Include optional opaque object ids; false when left out. Required references and positions remain.

name: edit_document
title: Edit a document
description: Create or change a shared document, as Markdown. One command per call. create: a new document in an existing writable document directory from list_shared, ending in the title you want and .md (for example "docs/Week 41.md"). Its parents must exist; use manage_shared create_folder to make a folder, and manage_shared copy to duplicate a document or folder. rewrite: replace a whole document with markdown. replace: put new in place of old, which must be the text exactly as you read it and occur once (or pass all). insert: add markdown after the block that contains after, or at the end when after is left out. rename: give it another title. describe: set its description, the line shown beside its title where documents are listed (create takes one too). attach: read one whole file relative to your thread's directory and store it in the document; paths outside the environment are refused. name defaults to its last path component; overwrite: true replaces an existing name while keeping its links. The environment must be online, and the file must fit the same per-file and total document limits as a person's upload. detach: remove a file by its stored name and any blocks showing it. File changes are named in the document's history under your thread. Read the document first and pass the seq you read it at as seq, so that you do not undo what somebody wrote meanwhile; rewrite requires it. People see every change at once, under your name, and can put an earlier version back. Name a shared thing as a Markdown link or in backquotes: its path or id:<id>, with #n for a part as read_shared counts it, for example [Rollout plan](<docs/Rollout plan.md#3>) (angle brackets around a path with spaces or parentheses). People see a chip, and the answer lists each reference resolved and each kept as text. Keep shared names followed by (no access) as they are: you may not read those references. Files also use a shared path or your workspace path, with :n or #n for a text line. Use your file tools for workspace paths.

command.description: What to do: create, rewrite, replace, insert, rename, describe, attach or detach.

path.description: One text document path or id. For create: a new path in an existing writable docs root or document folder, ending in the title and .md. Use manage_shared for folders and copies.

markdown.description: The text, as Markdown: for create, rewrite and insert.

ids.description: Include optional opaque object ids; false when left out. Required references and positions remain.

old.description: For replace: the text to put something in place of, exactly as read_shared gave it.

new.description: For replace: the text to put there.

all.description: For replace: change every place old occurs, not only a single one.

after.description: For insert: text in the block the new text follows. At the end when left out.

description.description: For describe, and optionally for create: what the document is about, shown beside its title where documents are listed (its first line). Empty takes it away.

file.description: For attach: one whole file relative to your thread's directory, without .. or an absolute path; it must remain inside the environment's roots and fit the document's upload limits.

name.description: For attach: the stored name, defaulting to the source's last path component; for detach: the stored file name to remove. At most 200 characters, without slashes or control characters.

overwrite.description: For attach: replace a file of the same name, retaining its identity and links; otherwise a name conflict refuses the call.

seq.description: The seq of the read the change was written on, so that what somebody wrote meanwhile is not undone. rewrite requires it.

max_bytes.description: The most UTF-8 bytes in the complete answer: 20000 when left out, at most 40000.

name: manage_shared
title: Organize documents and folders
description: Organize shared documents and document folders using paths from list_shared. create_folder creates one empty folder at a new path inside an existing writable document directory. copy copies documents or complete folder trees into to, with fresh identities and history under destination creation access; source grants, comments and history are not copied. move relocates them while preserving identity, history and attached files. delete soft-deletes the complete selection, keeping it recoverable during retention. restore brings back deleted items or an earlier document version, preserving the text it replaces as a version. For copy and move, to must be an existing document directory; name optionally gives one source a new basename. No implicit parents, overwrite, automatic renaming, overlapping selections, or destination inside the source. Only delete requires two calls: first without confirm, read the complete preview including every descendant, files, history, audience changes and restoration deadline; then repeat exactly those arguments with its token. Request a new preview if it changed or expired. create_folder, copy, move and restore execute directly with no confirmation call. Every operation authorizes the whole tree and executes all or none. Built-in docs, attachment and history directories are not mutable objects. Use edit_document to create or change document content. These operations organize Orch documents, not your execution workspace.

command.description: What to do: create_folder, copy, move, delete or restore. Only delete uses preview and confirm.

paths.description: One to twenty document or document-folder paths or id references from list_shared. create_folder takes exactly one new folder path whose parent exists. At most fifty documents and folders, including all descendants, may be affected; overlapping selections are refused. restore also accepts a deleted item or one earlier document version.

to.description: Required for copy and move: an existing writable document directory. Parent directories are never created implicitly.

name.description: Optional new basename for copy or move with exactly one source; keep .md for a text document. No separators, overwrite or automatic renaming.

confirm.description: For delete only: repeat the same arguments with the confirmation token from the complete deletion preview. All other commands execute directly without confirm.

max_bytes.description: The most UTF-8 bytes in the complete answer: 20000 when left out, at most 40000.

ids.description: Include optional opaque object ids; false when left out. Required references and positions remain.

name: send_message
title: Send a message
description: Send text, files from your workspace, or both, to one typed target. target.kind "chat" posts visibly to the people in the chat at target.path, which list_shared must show as writable; reply_to optionally answers a message by its number from read_shared. It appears under your agent's name and notifies the chat's followers. Write there when asked, or to answer what was asked there; it is not a place for progress notes. target.kind "thread" hands a note to the agent of another thread at target.path: one in your topic by its unique name, or a shared path or id with write access. It follows that topic's delivery, fallback and wake policies; it may wait for the next turn and does not necessarily start one. reply_to is refused for threads. Files are relative workspace paths without .., at most 10; an unreadable, outside or oversized file refuses the whole message. A thread's files are stored whole and delivered into its directory. The result names the resolved target and files: status "posted" means the chat message is stored; status "queued" means the thread note is stored, with delivery "deferred", "queued", "steered" or "interrupted" describing the scheduled action, not an acknowledgement from its agent. To tell every thread on the topic use announce. Name a shared thing as a Markdown link or in backquotes, its path or id:<id> with #n for a part, for example [Rollout plan](<docs/Rollout plan.md#3>); readers see a chip, and the answer lists each reference resolved and each kept as text. Literal @all stays plain text. Each target retains its own write permissions and message quota. Do not send what was not asked for. Files also use a shared path or your workspace path, with :n or #n for a text line. Use your file tools for workspace paths.

target.description: The intended recipient. Chat paths name chat.md; thread paths name a thread or its conversation.md. Each kind keeps its own write permissions.

kind.description: Who receives the message: people in a chat, or the agent of another thread.

path.description: The shared path or id: and an id of the chat or thread. A thread of your own topic may also be named by its unique name.

files.description: Files in your directory to attach, as relative paths without ..; at most 10. The whole message is refused if a file cannot be read or exceeds the attachment limit.

reply_to.description: For a chat target only: the number of the message this answers, as read_shared shows it. Omit it for a thread.

max_bytes.description: The most UTF-8 bytes in the complete answer: 20000 when left out, at most 40000.

ids.description: Include optional opaque object ids; false when left out. Required references and positions remain.

name: announce
title: Announce
description: Tell everybody on the work about something that happened in yours. category "notice" (the default) is for a finding the other agents on this topic need in order to act: a root cause, a changed interface, a blocker. It is delivered into their threads, where each reads it as a colleague's note. category "milestone" is for a point of progress that the people following your thread should hear of; it goes to them alone and enters no other agent's work. Keep the body to what they need, at most 1500 characters; put anything longer in a document or a file and name it. Use it rarely, and never announce again something that reached you as an announcement. To tell one thread, use send_message with target.kind "thread" and its path. Link a shared or workspace path, or id:<id>, with #n for a part: [Rollout plan](<docs/Rollout plan.md#3>). Each receiving agent gets its own paths; the answer lists references resolved or kept as text.

body.description: The rest: what the others need in order to act.

audience.description: Who hears it: followers, topic, project or the nearest org, within the place's announcement reach. A notice goes to the topic and a milestone to the followers unless this says otherwise.

severity.description: info (the default), or important, which also reaches the people who asked to hear only of what matters: keep it for what stops their work.

delivery.description: How it reaches a thread at work: interrupt, steer or next_turn. Honoured only where the topic lets agents choose.

wake_idle.description: Whether it starts a turn on a thread that is idle. Honoured only where the topic lets agents choose.

max_bytes.description: The most UTF-8 bytes in the complete answer: 20000 when left out, at most 40000.

ids.description: Include optional opaque object ids; false when left out. Required references and positions remain.

name: request_capability
title: Ask for a capability
description: Ask for an environment capability you lack (for example KVM). Your instructions list what this environment has and what it can be given; a name it does not know is answered with that list. reason says in a sentence what you need it for; a person may read it before deciding. If it is granted the environment is recreated: running processes stop, the workspace and home directory are kept, and you are told when it is ready.

capability.description: The key of the capability, as your instructions list it.

reason.description: What you need it for, in a sentence; a person may read it before deciding.

max_bytes.description: The most UTF-8 bytes in the complete answer: 20000 when left out, at most 40000.

ids.description: Include optional opaque object ids; false when left out. Required references and positions remain.

name: use_browser
title: Open or announce a browser
description: Get a web browser that the people on this work can watch and drive with you, or tell them of one you started. Browsers run in your environment; a profile is a named directory there that keeps the sign-ins made in it, and a profile has one running browser at a time. list: the profiles, the browsers that run and where each is driven (its endpoint, an address on 127.0.0.1), and what is installed to drive one. open: a browser on a profile; give profile to use one by its name (one that somebody signed in to, for example; it is made if it does not exist), or leave it out for a profile of your thread's own. If a browser already runs on that profile you get that one: share it, and work in tabs you open yourself. preset "window" starts it with a window on a display, for a site that turns away a browser without one. The answer has the endpoint and, in attach, the command that connects to it with what is installed here. announce: you started a browser yourself, with an address for driving on 127.0.0.1; give its endpoint so that people see it. close: a browser you opened or announced, when you are done with it; a profile keeps its sign-ins. When a page needs a person (a sign-in, a code, a captcha), say so in your answer and name the browser: they open it from the conversation, do it, and tell you. Never type a password yourself that you were not given for that purpose.

command.description: List, open or join, announce, or close a browser.

profile.description: Kept profile name; open makes it when missing. Omit for your thread's own.

preset.description: Full browser without a window, or on a display.

url.description: First page of a newly opened browser.

endpoint.description: The loopback HTTP address of a browser you started with --remote-debugging-port=0.

browser.description: The identifier of a browser you opened or announced, to close.

note.description: A short line for people about the browser you open or announce.

name: use_display
title: Open or announce a display
description: Get a graphical display that the people on this work can watch and work in with you, or tell them of one you started. Use it for a program that has to show a window: a desktop application, an emulator, a browser with a window. list: the displays that are served and where. open: a virtual screen of the size you give as geometry (for example "1280x800"); the answer has its X display, which you set as DISPLAY for the programs you start on it, and its endpoint. announce: you started something that serves VNC yourself, on 127.0.0.1 or on a socket; give its endpoint, and its password if it has one, so that people see it. close: one you opened or announced. A display shows whatever is on it to everybody who may watch this environment's displays: keep secrets off it.

command.description: Choose list to read the displays, open for a new virtual screen, announce for your own local VNC server, or close for a display this thread opened or announced.

name.description: Listed name for a new virtual screen.

endpoint.description: Loopback VNC port or local socket path to announce.

password.description: The announced server's password, kept sealed and given to no viewer.

display.description: Identifier of a display you opened or announced, to close.

note.description: A short purpose line for people.

name: list_ports
title: List the environment's ports
description: List ports of your own environment: local TCP listeners and bound UDP sockets, the program where known, and openings for other people with their current state, address and transports. Give port to get its stable browser address before the program starts. The answer names the audiences this place allows, its limit and current use, and how a caller can arrive by browser, helper or host. It includes openings requested by other threads here. A bound UDP socket may only send; the answer does not pretend it is a server. It opens, changes and closes nothing. No access ticket, personal token or undisclosed link is returned.

port.description: A port of the environment, also one no program listens on yet, to learn its address.

limit.description: How many rows: 50 when left out.

cursor.description: Where a list that was cut goes on: the cursor it gave.

max_bytes.description: The most UTF-8 bytes in the complete answer: 20000 when left out, at most 40000.

ids.description: Include optional opaque object ids; false when left out. Required references and positions remain.

name: open_port
title: Ask to open a port
description: Ask to open one environment port to a named place, a link holder or callers at the host. Give port, kind and a reason a person reads. Omit place_id for your own topic, or name another readable place; until and entry_methods apply to a link; host_port fixes a host number. transports selects TCP, UDP or both. program says HTTP or HTTPS inside and an expected Host when your dev server refuses the outside name; otherwise Host is passed. Its TCP PROXY choice needs a dedicated program port expecting that header on every connection, including your own trials; UDP has no PROXY. It opens at once where this environment holds that kind's capability (port_place, port_link, port_host) or its place's policy allows it; otherwise a current Ports manager decides, and may grant the capability. The call waits up to one minute and answers its current admission and availability with what happens next. A late decision reaches this thread and starts no turn. Repeating the same request makes no second opening or card; a refusal lasts an hour. An agent-requested link is sent to this thread unless its decider chooses For me only; the card says so before approval. A browser link gives a ready webhook URL; keep its orch_token query when adding your service path.

port.description: The port of the environment the program listens on: never a process or an outside address.

kind.description: Who is let in: the viewers of a place, whoever holds a link, or whoever reaches the host.

place_id.description: With kind place: the place whose viewers are let in, by an id list_shared gave; this thread's topic when left out.

label.description: With kind link: a readable name for the link, which is no secret.

transports.description: tcp, udp or both: both for host and helper, tcp for a browser, when left out.

entry_methods.description: With kind link only: browser, helper or both; both where the domain exists, helper alone otherwise, when left out.

until.description: With kind link, and then required: when the link ends, an absolute time within the allowed maximum.

host_port.description: With kind host: a fixed outside port, in the range the host allows.

program.description: How the program inside is spoken to, all three members as list_ports gives them; the current ones when left out.

http_scheme.description: Whether the program speaks HTTP or HTTPS inside; its certificate is not checked.

host_header.description: The Host header the program needs, where a development server asks for one; null otherwise.

proxy_protocol.description: Whether TCP connections begin with the PROXY protocol, for a program that reads it.

reason.description: One sentence the deciding person reads: what it is for.

max_bytes.description: The most UTF-8 bytes in the complete answer: 20000 when left out, at most 40000.

ids.description: Include optional opaque object ids; false when left out. Required references and positions remain.

name: close_port
title: Close a port's opening
description: Close an opening this thread asked for, using its opening reference. It ends its TCP connections and UDP associations and does not open again at a restart. No new person decision is needed. Repeating close returns the same closed opening. Another thread or person’s opening is refused with who may close it. To inspect first, use list_ports; to see callers, use list_port_connections.

opening.description: The opening to close, as list_ports or open_port named it.

max_bytes.description: The most UTF-8 bytes in the complete answer: 20000 when left out, at most 40000.

ids.description: Include optional opaque object ids; false when left out. Required references and positions remain.

name: list_port_connections
title: List who reached a port
description: List callers using ports of your own environment now or recently. Narrow by opening, by the listener port, by transport, or by inside_port, the peer port your program logged. Each row has outside caller address and port, the proved person by username or link by label where known, and the separate inside address and port your program sees. It gives since, last active, bytes each way and HTTP request count where applicable, plus bounded totals by caller and their tracking time. It includes other threads’ openings here. PROXY being off changes none of these facts. It contains no traffic, header, assertion, access ticket or personal token. It changes nothing.

opening.description: Only the connections through this opening, as list_ports or open_port named it.

port.description: Only the connections to this port of the environment.

inside_port.description: Only the connection your program saw come from this port, to match a line of its log.

limit.description: How many rows: 50 when left out.

cursor.description: Where a list that was cut goes on: the cursor it gave.

max_bytes.description: The most UTF-8 bytes in the complete answer: 20000 when left out, at most 40000.

ids.description: Include optional opaque object ids; false when left out. Required references and positions remain.

name: goal
title: Report on the goal
description: Your goal on this thread: the work you were given and the condition, "Done when", that ends it. command get returns the objective, the condition, the limits, what has been used and your earlier reports. command update reports where you stand when you stop working for now, in one call: status working, with next saying what you will do; met, with evidence saying what you ran or read and what it showed, which proves the condition holds; or blocked, with evidence saying what stops you and next saying what you need, when only a person can go on. Orch checks a report of met against the condition; where the evidence does not show it you are told why at the start of your next turn and go on. Example: {"command":"update","status":"met","evidence":"npm test: 212 passed, 0 failed, run at the end of this turn in /work"}.

command.description: get reads the goal; update reports where you stand.

status.description: With update: working while you go on, met when the condition holds, blocked when only a person can go on.

evidence.description: With update and status met or blocked, required: what you ran or read and what it showed, or what stops you.

next.description: With update: what you will do next, or what you need from a person.
